justification:
CVE-2025-24849 affected the Dario Health Android application, where the app lacked encryption in transit for its cloud infrastructure, facilitating potential sensitive data manipulation or exposure (CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information, CVSS 7.1 HIGH). The app transmitted sensitive health data to its servers without TLS encryption, allowing adjacent network attackers to intercept data in plaintext.

The synthetic vulnerability in Funkwhale for Android replicates this same weakness class. Funkwhale is a music streaming client that connects to a self-hosted server over HTTPS (port 443) to authenticate users via OAuth 2.0 and stream audio content. The app includes a cleartext traffic option for development purposes, but by default enforces HTTPS when no URL scheme is specified and validates that users cannot accidentally use HTTP URLs.

The vulnerability patch introduces three changes:

1. In LoginActivity.kt, the URL scheme selection is modified to always use 'http://' when no scheme is provided, regardless of the cleartext toggle setting. The original code defaults to 'https://' when cleartext is not explicitly enabled.

2. In LoginActivity.kt, the hostname validation that rejects 'http://' URLs when cleartext mode is disabled is removed, allowing HTTP connections to proceed without warning.

3. In AndroidManifest.xml, the android:networkSecurityConfig attribute is removed. On Android 9+ (API 28+), when a network security config is present, it overrides the android:usesCleartextTraffic manifest attribute and blocks cleartext HTTP by default. By removing the networkSecurityConfig reference, the existing android:usesCleartextTraffic='true' attribute takes effect, permitting the downgraded HTTP connections to proceed.

The result is that when a user enters a server hostname without a scheme (the common case), the app silently connects over plaintext HTTP instead of HTTPS. All subsequent API traffic — including OAuth client registration (client_id and client_secret), authorization tokens, and audio streaming requests — is transmitted in cleartext, visible to any attacker on the adjacent network.

Both CVE-2025-24849 and this synthetic vulnerability demonstrate the same fundamental security flaw: a mobile application transmitting sensitive data to its server infrastructure without encryption. The attack vector (adjacent network interception), impact (exposure of authentication credentials and personal data), and root cause (CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information) are consistent across both vulnerabilities.
